Just as President Donald J. Trump predicted, gas prices are tumbling down — and American families are feeling the relief just in time for Thanksgiving. From coast to coast, prices at the pump are falling fast, with the national average falling to its lowest price in eight months after the biggest three-week dive since 2008. As millions of Americans hit the road to gather with the people they love, President Trump is delivering just what he promised: real relief at the pump and more money in families’ pockets this holiday season.

Today, President Donald J. Trump stood with the families of murder victims to condemn Gov. Gavin Newsom’s gutless decision to wipe out the death sentences of all 548 inmates on California’s death row. Two days after the election, Newsom handed blanket clemency to child killers, serial murderers, and cop killers, and the victims’ families say they were never even told — a shameful abdication of basic responsibility and integrity that defines today’s Democrat Party.

  • “Face me, Gov. Newsom. Tell me Michael’s life doesn’t matter. Michael deserved a Governor who would stand with the victims, honor their justice, and respect the will of the people. You may have taken our justice, but you will never take Michael’s voice,” said Sandy Friend, whose son, Michael Lyons, was kidnapped, tortured, and brutally murdered at just 8-years-old.
  • “For three decades, our family lived with the understanding that the justice system’s decision would stand. Today, I stand before you outraged — outraged — that Gov. Gavin Newsom unilaterally erased that sentence,” said Marc Klaas, whose 12-year-old daughter, Polly, was abducted at knifepoint and strangled.
  • “Gov. Newsom, under the cloak of darkness, unilaterally makes a decision to commute the sentences of the most heinous criminals in our society. I am disgusted and frustrated. My brother did not die in vain,” said Lt. Jason Davis, whose brother was killed in the line of duty by a depraved illegal alien.
  • “My dad was more than a police officer. He was a loving father, a grandfather, a public servant, and a friend to many. I am incredibly proud to be his daughter, and his love, sacrifice, and legacy will stay with me forever,” said Gloria Vega, whose father, Officer Jose “Gil” Vega, was murdered in the line of duty just months before he was set to retire.

Meet the Monsters Newsom Is Fighting to Spare:

  • Marcus Wesson murdered nine of his own children and grandchildren — the youngest just a year old — and raped and molested his daughters and nieces inside the cult-like family he controlled for years.
  • Richard Allen Davis snatched 12-year-old Polly Klaas at knifepoint from a slumber party in her own home and strangled her.
  • Isauro Aguirre tortured 8-year-old Gabriel Fernandez for months, then beat him to death — leaving him with a fractured skull, a dozen broken ribs, and burns.
  • David Westerfield kidnapped 7-year-old Danielle van Dam from her own San Diego bedroom and murdered her.
  • Charles Ng tortured and sexually abused women on videotape at a remote Sierra foothills cabin and slaughtered 11 people — including two baby boys.
  • Randy Kraft murdered 16 young men, sexually mutilating them and dumping their bodies along Southern California freeways before police caught him with a dead Marine in his passenger seat.
  • Chester Turner raped and strangled 14 women in South Los Angeles over more than a decade, becoming the city’s most prolific serial killer.
  • Vincent Brothers slaughtered his wife, Joanie, her mother, and their three children — Marques, 4, Lyndsey, 2, and 6-week-old Marshall — in their Bakersfield home.
  • Ramon Salcido slit the throats of his daughters Sofia, 4, and Teresa, 1, then murdered his wife, her mother, her two young sisters, and a co-worker.
  • Cary Stayner murdered Carole Sund, her 15-year-old daughter, Juli, and 16-year-old Silvina Pelosso near Yosemite in 1999.
  • Luis Bracamontes, a twice-deported killer, gunned down Sacramento County Deputy Danny Oliver and Placer County Detective Michael Davis, Jr., in 2014 — then told the court he wished he had killed more.
  • Daniel Wozniak shot his neighbor, 26-year-old Army veteran Sam Herr, to bankroll his own wedding, dismembered his body, then lured Herr’s friend Julie Kibuishi, 23, and murdered her to frame him.

That Newsom would even consider sparing these killers tells you everything you need to know about the sickness and depravity that runs through the Democrat Party.

As millions of Americans prepare to travel for the Thanksgiving holiday, President Donald J. Trump is making sure the skies stay open and the systems run smoothly. Under President Trump’s leadership, the White House has assembled an elite, interagency team to keep America’s air traffic control systems strong and reliable throughout the holiday season.

From The Daily Wire:

“As Americans prepare for Thanksgiving travel, the White House has assembled a special team to prevent any further air traffic control outages, officials shared with The Daily Wire.

The White House assembled the ‘Transportation Technology Transformation Tiger Team’ in the wake of a malfunction that resulted in a grounding of all flights nationwide. The team — comprised of officials from the FAA, Departments of Transportation and Defense, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence — has met every day this week to ensure continuity of service, a White House official shared…

White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster tells The Daily Wire Americans preparing to hit the road this week have nothing to worry about.

‘President Trump and [Transportation] Secretary [Sean] Duffy have brought together the best and the brightest across the government to ensure what happened last Friday can never happen again,’ Schuster said. ‘Work continues, and Americans can rest assured their country’s aviation is the best in the world.’”

President Donald J. Trump will celebrate a uniquely American Thanksgiving tradition as the White House hosts the 79th National Thanksgiving Turkey presentation and pardoning ceremony on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

This year’s turkeys, named Freedom and Feathers by the American people via an online poll last week, were raised in West Virginia, under the direction of National Turkey Federation Chairwoman Christy Puffenbarger, by owners of Deans Gap Farm Scott and Becky Rightsell.

Each year, two turkeys are officially pardoned by the President of the United States, but only one receives the ceremonial honor at the White House. Following a final public poll on WhiteHouse.Gov/Thanksgiving, one of these two turkeys will be ceremonially pardoned at the White House on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Both turkeys will live out their days at Texas A&M following the ceremony.

The American public is now invited to decide which turkey will take center stage during the pardon ceremony hosted by President Trump by voting here.

Voting will conclude the night of Monday, November 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM.

In a White House press briefing today, President Donald J. Trump took questions from reporters alongside Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Fresh off his return from Asia, President Trump used the briefing to underscore that America is negotiating from a position of restored strength — highlighting more than $17 billion in deals that put American workers, farmers, and families first. He also made clear that he is ready to work across the aisle, especially on healthcare, to deliver results for the American people.

  • On the historic Asia trip: “Last night, we returned home from one of the most successful presidential visits to Asia in American history… In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals and about ten others coming very soon, attended four major international summits, reaffirmed America’s alliances throughout the region, and advanced the cause of peace and security around the world.” (Watch)
  • On working with Democrats: “Because of the power of the veto, there’s a real possibility that we’ll get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare. I’m open to great healthcare. Now, can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want — and we could end up with great healthcare in our country.” (Watch)
  • On trade with Thailand: “Thailand signed an agreement to eliminate all tariffs on American products… and remove their non-tariff barriers, and they want to buy $2.6 billion a year in U.S. agricultural products, and we’re going to increase that number… Our farmers are a big beneficiary of this trip.” (Watch)
  • On trade with the Philippines: “Philippine Airlines will purchase… 20 brand new Boeing 787 Dreamliners with General Electric engines. It’s a big contract, supporting 47,000 American jobs.” (Watch)
  • On permitting reform: “Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It’s one of the biggest things that you will see. It’s a big deal… Now, it goes to the House — and if passed, it’s projected to put at least $1,300/year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans. But it’s even beyond that; it’s going to cause tremendous amounts of new building.” (Watch)
  • On the trilateral summit and nuclear security: “We discussed the responsibility of the world’s three largest nuclear powers… to reduce the risk that these weapons pose to the world… We spoke about the need to cooperate to stop the proliferation of that nuclear threat throughout our planet. And in particular, we talked extensively about ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” (Watch)
  • On meeting President Putin: “I held a bilateral meeting with President Putin of Russia, who clearly expressed his desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end by diplomatic means.” (Watch)
  • On economic strength: “The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength… Already, gasoline is down 60 cents a gallon from just one month ago, and it’s going to be dropping fast.” (Watch)
  • On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me. We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they’ve been doing for 51 years… They’ve been bullshitting people for 51 years.” (Watch)
  • On American strength: “Everywhere I went on this trip and every leader I met, it was clear that America is respected again like never before. We are respected.” (Watch)
  • On keeping critical infrastructure in America: “Whoever wins SI wins… We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We’re not going to allow that to happen. You know, they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else and it was very destructive to our country… We want them to build it here.” (Watch)

“Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It’s one of the biggest things that you will see. It’s a big deal… It’s projected to put at least $1,300 a year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans.” – President Donald J. Trump

President Donald J. Trump is committed to fixing America’s broken permitting system — standing behind the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), legislation that will modernize federal environmental reviews and permitting while delivering cheaper energy, high-paying jobs, and economic growth across the United States.

Last night, the Senate advanced landmark permitting reform legislation, and now the House has the opportunity to finish the job and send the bill to President Trump’s desk to lock in generations of affordability and energy dominance for the American people. 

Here’s what they’re saying about the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

American Exploration & Production Council CEO Anne Bradbury: “AXPC applauds the Senate for taking decisive bipartisan action to remove longstanding barriers to American energy and infrastructure development. BAAJA offers a generational opportunity to cut through permitting delays and lower costs across America without compromising critical environmental protections. With meaningful relief for American families within reach, we respectfully urge the House to send BAAJA to the President’s desk before the end of the year.” 

American Chemistry Council: “Yesterday’s vote represents an important step toward addressing longstanding permitting challenges that have delayed projects, increased costs, and hindered economic growth. As demand for energy, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure continues to grow, the United States needs a permitting system capable of supporting investment and development at the speed required to compete globally. 

“The future of American manufacturing, infrastructure, and energy development depends on our nation’s ability to build. Enactment of this legislation would help ensure the United States remains the best place in the world to invest, manufacture, and innovate “

American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers: “Today’s bipartisan Senate vote marks a major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure. We thank Senators Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich for advancing long-overdue reforms.”  

Association of American Railroads CEO and President Ian Jefferies: “Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an encouraging step toward a permitting process that works better for communities and the projects they depend on. Freight railroads make long-term investments in the network that connects businesses, farms, ports, and consumers. When reviews take years, needed improvements can be delayed. This bipartisan legislation can help make project reviews timelier and more predictable while preserving important environmental protections.”

Business Roundtable CEO Joshua Bolten: “Business Roundtable applauds the Senate for passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. The strong bipartisan vote marks an important step toward enacting comprehensive permitting reforms that would help lower costs for American families and businesses. 

“By modernizing the federal permitting system, this legislation would make it easier to build critical energy projects, roads, ports and other much-needed infrastructure. The benefits would flow to Americans in the form of lower utility bills, new good-paying jobs and more private-sector investment in communities across the country. We urge the House to finish the job and swiftly pass this measure.”

Interstate Natural Gas Association of America President and CEO Amy Andryszak: “Tonight’s Senate vote marks a pivotal step toward modernizing America’s permitting process and ensuring affordable energy for American consumers. Enshrining improvements to the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), judicial reviews, and permit certainty in statute will help accelerate the buildout of the critical energy infrastructure needed to meet growing demand and ensure a reliable, affordable energy future. 

“We applaud Senators for reaching bipartisan consensus and urge the U.S. House of Representatives to act quickly to send this legislation to the President’s desk. The House must pass this legislation without further delay to help meet America’s energy needs and address rising energy costs.”

Laborers International Union of North America President Brent Booker: “For more than a decade, endless permitting delays have stalled critical infrastructure projects that put our members to work across the country. Every month a project sits on the shelf, LIUNA members go without paychecks. This bill ends the runaround. It sets clear timelines and holds the process accountable, so projects get decided and built. Congress has spent years talking about the need to fix our broken permitting process. Now it has a real opportunity to do something about it. The cost of inaction is too high: lost jobs, lost investment, and lost opportunities for working Americans. We cannot afford to let another Congress come and go while critical projects remain stalled and working families pay the price.” 

National Association of Home Builders: “With so many families priced out of the market, the House must pass this bill without delay. BAAJA will make federal permits faster and less costly for builders and developers, lowering land development costs and making lots more affordable. It also helps multifamily developers by ensuring that the use of federal grants and loans does not automatically trigger a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review. For projects that still need a NEPA review, the bill sets enforceable deadlines for agencies to complete it.”

National Electrical Manufacturers Association President and CEO Debra Phillips: “America’s electricity needs are growing rapidly, and this legislation will help us build the infrastructure to meet them. It speeds up transmission projects, encourages grid-enhancing advanced transmission technologies, and gives investors more certainty, which means more reliable, affordable power for consumers. That will help America build the energy system our future demands, and move past an outdated permitting system that has been tangled in red tape for too long. We commend the bipartisan leadership that made this progress possible and urge the House to finish the job.”

National Mining Association President and CEO Rich Nolan: “We’re grateful to the Senate for coming together to move legislation that will help transform American potential into American production, and for the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich, who deserve great credit for their tireless work to advance the bill. True economic and national security comes with a United States that can build things again, using domestic materials and domestic fuels, and decisively confront China’s supply chain dominance. It’s now up to the House to say American prosperity and competitiveness matter, ensure that made in America can also be mined in America, and pass this legislation.”

National Rural Electric Cooperative Association CEO Jim Matheson: “This legislation will dramatically improve the federal permitting system, making it more manageable and predictable for electric co-ops as they work to keep the lights on at a cost families and businesses can afford. Today’s environmental review processes can take years, delaying critical energy projects and increasing costs that ultimately fall on consumers.  The bill will streamline reviews and reduce litigation delays, while leaving important environmental protections in place.”

U.S. Oil and Gas Association President Tim Stewart: “BAAJA brought together the broadest and most diverse coalition of working interests that Washington has seen in decades who worked to pass a good piece of legislation that will let us build things in America again. 

“It will ensure greater abundance and affordability for the next generation and we are proud to be a part of it.”

Western Energy Alliance: “We have a generational choice in front of us. We must decide if we’re going to be builders or not. If we’re going to meet our nation’s energy needs, or not. Reforming the nation’s outdated permitting system is critical to delivering affordable energy and growing jobs. Our nation’s economy can no longer sustain the strategy of activist groups to defer, delay, and deny high-value energy and infrastructure projects. This bill is an important step toward providing greater certainty, while still prioritizing the environment. It broadly benefits infrastructure development and all sources of energy production. We’re pleased to see senators come together in bipartisan manner to work out key differences for the benefit of the American people. We now urge lawmakers in the House to take the deal and deliver a win on energy affordability before the current session ends.”

Yesterday, President Donald J. Trump named Kirsten A. Davies to lead the White House Office of the National Cyber Director. A battle-tested cyber leader and the Pentagon’s Chief Information Officer, Davies will drive an America First cyber strategy that treats cybersecurity as national security and keeps the United States dominant and secure in cyberspace.

Her selection immediately drew praise from leaders across the Administration:

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: “The Department congratulates Kirsten Davies on her new role as the National Cyber Director. Throughout her tenure at DOW, she has proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional, and we are confident she will advance President Trump’s America First agenda across the cybersecurity landscape.”

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton: “With nearly two decades of leadership experience in the technology space, Kirsten Davies will be a strong asset for the Trump administration in her new position with the Office of the National Cyber Director. It has been my pleasure to work closely with Kirsten on national security matters, and I look forward to now working with her to navigate an increasingly dynamic and fast-moving cyber landscape.”

Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy Michael Kratsios: “Congratulations @_KirstenDavies_, our new National Cyber Director. Kirsten brings deep cyber expertise and a proven record from her time in industry and at the Department of War. Cybersecurity is vital to our nation’s security and prosperity, and I look forward to working together to strengthen it.”

Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata: “Great pick. Congrats @_KirstenDavies_. Look forward to continuing to work together.”

Director of External Engagements for the Department of War CIO Marci McCarthy: “Congratulations, @Kirsten_Davies_! Having worked alongside you, I’ve witnessed firsthand your extraordinary leadership, vision, and unwavering commitment to strengthening our nation’s cybersecurity and national security. Proud to call you both my boss and my great friend. America’s cyber future is in great hands!”

National Defense University Cyber Scholar JD Work: “Congratulations. A superb choice for many reasons, foremost in technical excellence and deep executive competence solving for some of the hardest problems ever faced in the cyber domain.”

President Trump has made cybersecurity a core pillar of his Administration. Under his leadership, the United States has:

  • Released a Cyber Strategy for America built on six pillars to keep the United States unrivaled in cyberspace, on offense and defense;
  • Overhauled cybersecurity for America’s military and intelligence systems, holding agency heads accountable and modernizing oversight for the first time in over 35 years;
  • Seized Chinese state-sponsored hacking platforms targeting U.S. critical infrastructure, including NASA and the Federal Reserve;
  • Unleashed vetted American companies, under federal oversight, to go after foreign cybercriminal networks;
  • Mandated post-quantum cryptography for high-value federal systems by 2030;
  • Harnessed AI to defend federal and military networks, creating a clearinghouse to find and patch vulnerabilities;
  • Ordered a plan to dismantle the transnational criminal networks and scam centers preying on Americans;
  • Charged 12 Chinese contract hackers and law enforcement officers behind global hacking campaigns that hit U.S. agencies;
  • Sanctioned ransomware enablers First VPN, Media Land, Aeza Group, and Zservers;
  • Blocked new foreign-made consumer routers deemed a national security threat;
  • Hardened federal software, internet routing, and encryption standards against foreign threats;
  • Signed laws funding the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, authorizing Cyber Command operations, and extending legal protections for companies that share cyber threat intelligence; and
  • Taken decisive first-term action, releasing the first fully articulated national cyber strategy in 15 years, elevating U.S. Cyber Command, creating CISA, securing the tech supply chain from foreign adversaries, ripping out untrusted telecom equipment, and purging untrusted software from federal systems.

The Trump Administration sees no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio made clear that these are separate incidents caused by companies patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems, with America leading the effort to harden its digital infrastructure.

  • DNI Clayton: “This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state. We’ve looked very closely. Anytime we see something like this, those are the first questions that we ask on behalf of the American people, and we go across and we say, ‘Is that what’s going on here?’ That is not what’s going on here.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other. In essence, the Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago… We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation-state, with a malign actor of any kind.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that because we know those things exist, and we’ve been looking for them in the past.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “People are fearful, people are uncertain — and the best way to deal with people’s uncertainty and discomfort is to share with them transparently what we know and what we believe in terms of the information we have before us… We are not under systemic attack… Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country… The American people should have confidence in that.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Let me tell you what we think this is, and we think that it is with confidence. Lots of institutions, because these vulnerabilities have been identified, are patching. They’re taking their systems down, they’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place… This is being done on much larger scale because everybody, and it’s a good news story, everybody recognizes it’s time to upgrade their systems. And as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases. And in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected. But this is just an upgrade in patching, an upgrade in systems.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you’ve identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption in the way your system works… Companies, which is a good thing, are now immediately sharing vulnerabilities because they don’t want to be accused of covering up something.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “As a result of SI and the ability to scan systems more quickly, the ability to identify vulnerabilities has increased. That is why it is so incumbent upon all of us to work together to patch, to report vulnerabilities, and it is where the U.S. is leading.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Our systems need upgrades. They need patching. We have legacy systems, and they’re more and more interconnected, and they’re handling more and more traffic… Thankfully, the U.S. is leading and is far ahead in that step change in technology… We’re going to come out the other side much better.” (Watch)

While Democrats shamefully lie and resist finishing the job, Secretary Duffy also reiterated that the $12.5 billion provided in the Working Families Tax Cuts (which not a single Democrat voted for) was written specifically for radar, radios, and related upgrades — not a new telecom network or software. As President Donald J. Trump made clear, Congress must approve the rest of the funding so the modernization can be finished.

Key exchanges:

I want everybody to work on this’ — because the safety of the traveling public is number one for him, like it is for me.” (State of the Union)
  • On what caused the ground stop: “The telecom in El Dorado, it was an old copper wire that basically was going to be decommissioned. They said it can’t be used anymore, so we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber and we brought in our routers and did the work, and that’s when we saw the flooding of the network.” (Face the Nation)
  • On the need for Congress to fully fund a modernized air traffic control network: “I have systems that are from the ‘90s. I have radar that are from the ‘60s and ‘70s… [We’re] replacing radar and radios, we’re putting in voice switches, we’re doing all of this work with the $12.5 billion, but one of the biggest problems we continue to see is our network — and the architecture of our network is from 1980. We need a modern technology and architecture. I have AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen all ready to go. We have the architecture ready to build a state-of-the-art telecom system that will give us resiliency. All I need is the money to finish it.” (State of the Union)
  • On what the $12.5 billion downpayment can — and can’t — do: “When I asked for a massive amount of money to fix the system, what the Congress did is they said, ‘Okay, we’ll give you a partial funding, $12.5 billion,’ in the One Big Beautiful Bill, and they were very specific in how we spend it… But what I don’t have money for is a new telecom system. Our towers are old. Our air traffic controllers oftentimes don’t have elevators or HVAC… Their roofs leak. Let’s build a new system that is worthy to be called American.” (State of the Union)

We should be able to invest in new networks, invest in software. We can do all things; we don’t have to pick one versus the other.” (Fox News Sunday)
  • On the safety of American air travel: “It is the safest air system in the world, bar none… It’s going to remain safe. But let’s not lie to each other — we have to make investments into a network that has been neglected for decades.” (Meet the Press)

On Friday night, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin briefed reporters after a nationwide FAA ground stop caused by instability in the nation’s decades-old air traffic control systems. The failure stemmed from overloaded 1980s-era equipment, with zero evidence of a cyberattack. President Trump has already secured $12.5 billion toward a full rebuild; the Administration is urging Congress to provide the remaining funding so this never happens again.
 
On what happened — and how the FAA kept every flight safe:

  • Secretary Duffy: “At 3:36 p.m., we experienced instability for our radar and our communications in our centers and our TRACONs across the country… At that point, we issued a ground stop. We had over 3,500 airplanes in the air; they all engaged and, last time I looked, we had less than 400 in the airspace. As they were all coming into safely land, we navigated it with our well-known procedures that we have when these incidents happen… We didn’t lose all telecom. We didn’t lose all radar. But that instability, because of an abundance of caution and making sure we keep the American flyer safe, we did the ground stop.” (Watch)

On an air traffic control system stuck in the 1980s:

  • Secretary Duffy: “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system… The President, for the last year, has been asking Congress to fully fund a full build of a brand-new air traffic control system. We have TDM telecom; this is analog telecom. Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data… Because of that, we shut the system down. I have already replaced some of those switches with President Trump — and our new IP switches did not go down. It’s the old hardware that went down. I think the question for the American people is: do you want your Congress to fund this? President Trump has asked for the money, he has asked the Congress on a bipartisan approach to give us the resources to build a state-of-the-art air traffic control system. Let’s not do a patchwork fix to a system that’s critical to every single family.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “We have old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded… By the way, none of your networks run on 1980 technology. You all got fiber, state-of-the-art, high-speed networks… But not the FAA.” (Watch)

On reports of a cyberattack:

  • Secretary Mullin: “We have seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or an SI attack.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “There is nothing that indicates [a cyberattack]… It appears that this was mechanically driven; however, we’re still looking.” (Watch)

On years of delay and the need for full funding:

  • Secretary Duffy: “This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding. This is bipartisan; this is American. I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder; he’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people, but the President can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “This is a national security risk. We just saw what took place when we have vulnerabilities and we have old systems… Our air traffic control system is outdated, and it hasn’t been a priority from Congress… This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road.” (Watch)

On building a brand-new system — starting now:

  • Secretary Duffy: “I did get partial funding through One Big Beautiful Bill — I got $12.5 billion, and with that money, we are spending it and spending it well. But the Congress at the time knew that that was not going to be enough… We now have an opportunity in an emergency funding bill before the end of the year to give the money.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “This is not going to get done overnight… but when do you want to start it? America, when do you want to start building a brand-new system? Well, you have a team with President Trump that actually is building it right now, but we don’t have full funding.” (Watch)

President Trump will never stop delivering on his promises to Make America Great Again. Time and time again, he has defied the naysayers, achieving what they deem as impossible to deliver results that improve the lives of the American people. 

Exercising his executive authority, the President has: 

  • Executed a record-setting 147 Executive Orders in his first 100 days—more than any other President in history—and over 290 Executive Orders since January 2025, delivering on his promises of a more prosperous and secure America. 
  • Delivered the most secure border in history, enforcing an extraordinary crackdown on illegal immigration, resulting in negative net migration to the U.S. for the first time in over half a century.

    • Captured all of the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted fugitives — 2.5 times as many as the entire previous four-year Administration — and six of the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters.
  • Cracked down on fraud, waste, and corruption across the federal government at an unprecedented rate, and restored integrity to federal programs designed to help Americans in need.
    • Uncovered more than $260 billion in fraud of taxpayer dollars and stopped $72 billion a year, breaking up large-scale fraud schemes and seeing through that fraudsters are brought to justice.
    • The Trump Administration has stopped fraudulent payments before they go out the door, detected high-risk fraud trends, and shut down suspected fraudulent providers and retailers.
  • Ended illegal and discriminatory diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices across government, education, and the private sector. 
    • Reformed higher education by ending race-based discrimination in admissions and employment, DEI programming, and antisemitism.
    • Secured historic settlements of hundreds of millions with elite universities for their DEI practices, including Columbia, Brown, Cornell, the University of Virginia, Northwestern, and the University of North Carolina.
    • Restored equal treatment and equal opportunity under the law by eliminating race-based policies and practices to rebalance outcomes along racial lines.
    • Secured deals with six major hospital systems to end their transgender mutilization of minors, protecting America’s children.
  • Spearheaded a nuclear energy renaissance and restored America’s position as the world’s leading oil producer and exporter. 
    • Revolutionized and time-bound the nuclear regulatory process.Enabled four new advanced reactors to reach criticality by July 4th, 2026. Today, a total of five have achieved criticality following President Trump’s historic Executive Orders.Completed more than 700 nuclear-energy licensing actions that will supply Americans with tens of thousands of megawatts in energy.
    • Delivered the largest oil deal in the history of the world to secure America’s energy future.
  • Enacted President Trump’s record-shattering deregulation agenda, saving a family of four over $17,500—or $1.5 trillion total—in one year alone by cutting over 400 regulations.
    • Thanks to these cuts, the Trump Administration is the first in history to reduce the regulatory burden on the American people.

With more than two years to go, President Trump will not hesitate to use the power and authority of the Executive Branch to deliver historic victories for the American people.

Days after the midterms, caravans of illegal aliens are already marching north to the U.S. — and they’re counting on Democrats to let them in. Why wouldn’t they? Congressional Democrats are vowing to abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, stop deportations, and hand out amnesty while border-state Democrats cut off cooperation on immigration enforcement. It’s the same open borders agenda that unleashed the worst border crisis in American history, but President Donald J. Trump isn’t letting Democrats bring it back.

The caravan, in its own words:

  • “There might be a light at the end of the tunnel, a way for us to get in… We believe the Democrats will help us,” said a Nicaraguan migrant who had already been deported once from the United States.
  • “We know that the Democrats are not going to let a point as big as the Latino vote be lost and I think they are going to give us the opportunity to reach to our new homes,” said a migrant traveling with the caravan.
  • “We hear that […] now that Congress has changed, the border has to be open. We have faith in God that [Democrats] will help us,” said a migrant heading for the border.
  • “From what we’ve seen in the news, yes, that is [Democrats’] intention,” said a Guatemalan migrant traveling north.

Since the election, Democrats have reinforced those expectations:

  • Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (11/9/26): “ICE is way out of control. We need to put an end to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine.”
  • Rep. Ayanna Pressley (11/12/26): “With our new Democratic majority, we must defend our immigrant neighbors… abolish ICE, and extend TPS.”
  • Rep. Rashida Tlaib (11/10/26): “Abolish ICE now.”
  • Rep.-elect Claire Valdez (11/8/26): “We have the mandate to… abolish ICE.”
  • Rep. Delia Ramirez (11/8/26): “Together, we will dismantle DHS and abolish ICE.”
  • Rep. Pramila Jayapal (11/8/26): “Reining in ICE and getting ICE off of our streets is another massive priority…”
  • Rep. Ayanna Pressley (11/8/26): “Democrats have a mandate to abolish ICE, shut down detention centers…”
  • Rep. Juan Vargas (11/8/26): “We need the people that are being deported.”
  • Sen. Alex Padilla (11/4/26): “Americans have spoken. We’re sick of ICE and DHS’ lawlessness and cruelty. It’s time to rein them in…”

Border-state Democrats are already tearing down enforcement:

  • Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (11/6/26): Strict border enforcement “was a dog-and-pony show. It was political theater and nonsense.”
  • Texas Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin (11/9/26): “We need to make sure law enforcement is not aiding and abetting ICE here in Texas.”
  • Houston Mayor John Whitmire (11/9/26): “We will change our policy regarding contact with ICE… Elections matter.”
  • San Antonio Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones (11/6/26): “Elections matter.”
  • Austin Mayor Kirk Watson (11/6/26): “I’ve said Austin ‘cannot and will not play into or perpetuate a policy of fear’ when it comes to immigration… With the change in state leadership, I anticipate being able to better partner with the state on issues… including those related to civil immigration enforcement.”

President Trump shut the border down — and it’s staying shut:

  • President Donald J. Trump (11/12/26): “Here we go again! With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms – I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again. Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico… But they will not be accepted! MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED… There will be no leniency!”
  • White House Border Czar Tom Homan (11/11/26): “Congress may be more blue, Texas may be more blue, but the White House is red, bright red… These caravans [can] come to the border all they want. They’re not going to be released into the United States… We’re not giving one inch on this border.”
  • DHS General Counsel James Percival (11/12/26): “If they do reach the southern border, they’re going to find a Border Patrol that is extremely ready. The President is still the President. The midterms don’t change that — and we are very prepared to deal with this.”

On this Veterans Day, President Donald J. Trump stood among the fallen at Arlington National Cemetery and rendered our nation’s highest salute to the living who still carry the cost of freedom. In words that echoed across the quiet hills where generations of heroes rest, the Commander-in-Chief honored every Patriot who has worn the uniform — from the beaches of Normandy to the mountains of Afghanistan — vowing that “while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.”

In a solemn and stirring address, President Trump saluted America’s warriors:

  • “On Veterans Day, we reaffirm our undying gratitude to every Patriot who has answered the call of duty. We pay tribute to all of those who have won the wars and worn the uniform, who face the enemy, who have beaten the enemy at every turn, who have borne the burdens of fate and destiny to stand as our protection in battle.” (Watch)
  • “We thank Almighty God for the noble warriors of the United States Military who have always stepped forward so that America might always stay free. To every veteran here at Arlington and across the nation: today we render you the highest salute, we offer you our deepest respect and love, and we pledge you our utmost loyalty and devotion.” (Watch)
  • “Across every generation, American liberty has been preserved by legions of selfless Patriots who have raised their right hands and sworn an oath of flesh and blood for a cause whose full cost could not be measured in advance… Time and time again for 250 years, the American warrior has returned victorious, our Republic has triumphed, and today, our country is stronger than it has ever been before.” (Watch)
  • “A nation without heroes is like a sky without stars or a heaven without angels — but in America, we’ve never known that darkness because we have the men and women of America’s armed forces, our guiding lights, our greatest heroes, and our guardian angels.” (Watch)
  • “From the Patriots’ first stand at Lexington Green and the Concord Bridge to the blood-soaked battlefields that saved our nation, from the treacherous trenches of Europe to the deepest waters of the Pacific and the farthest reaches of the world, our veterans have answered every call, met every threat, crushed every foe, and borne every burden of war so that our children might know every single blessing of peace and love.” (Watch)
  • “America’s veterans have always fulfilled their duty to us, and while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.” (Watch)
  • “We say to every American veteran: the sacrifice you have made, we will never forget; the oath that you have kept, we will never take for granted; the values you fought for, we will never, ever forsake; the flag you held high, we will never let it fall; and the nation you served, we will never, ever let it fail.” (Watch)

President Trump also recognized living legends whose service spans generations, each a living testament to American valor:

  • On Cpl. Jack Myers, World War II: “At 19 years old, Jack Myers kissed his young bride and newborn son goodbye and went to serve as a gunner in the 692nd Tank Destroyer Battalion in World War II — brave people, all. In the frostbitten winter of 1944, Cpl. Myers found himself in the largest battle in American history, the Battle of the Bulge… Months later, Jack’s battalion was among the first to liberate the Dachau concentration camp, coming face to face with the evil he risked his life to destroy. Today, Jack is a great-great-grandfather and is here to receive our nation’s gratitude at 103 years old.” (Watch)
  • On Col. Douglas Moore, Vietnam: “U.S. Army Col. Douglas Moore served as one of the famous Dustoff medevac pilots in Vietnam — boy, could they fly — flying an incredible 1,874 combat missions and evacuating 2,782 badly wounded soldiers… For his actions, Douglas received our military’s second-highest honor, the Distinguished Service Cross. Over three decades, he also received two Distinguished Flying Crosses, a Bronze Star, and 33 Air Medals.” (Watch)
  • On SFC Ryan Hendrickson, Afghanistan: “In 2010, Green Beret Ryan Hendrickson was leading his team through a Taliban-held village in Afghanistan at three in the morning when he… stepped on enemy explosives — a lot of them. The blast ripped through his lower body, and he looked down to see his shattered bones protruding from his absolutely mangled leg and arm. Certain that he would die, Ryan’s only thought as he was airlifted away was the men he was leaving behind… They told him his combat career was over, but Ryan was not done. Eighteen months later, he returned to Afghanistan… For his courage, he was awarded the Silver Star.” (Watch)
  • On Marine veteran Dale Garner, Beirut: “As a young man, Dale Garner enlisted in the Marines after the Iran Hostage Crisis. Soon, he deployed to Beirut on a mission of peace — but on the morning of October 23, 1983, Iranian-backed Hezbollah terrorists… detonated a truck packed with explosives at the Marine barracks with hundreds of Americans inside… He was the sole survivor of the men around him, and he joins us here to remember the 241 American service members murdered in the Beirut barracks bombing, the deadliest day for the Marine Corps since Iwo Jima.” (Watch)

From the day he returned to the White House, President Trump has placed America’s veterans at the center of his agenda:

  • Lower drug costs: Prescription drug prices have posted their sharpest drop in more than 60 years, and the VA has secured more than $10 billion in pharmaceutical savings this fiscal year alone.
  • Faster benefits: President Trump signed an Executive Order modernizing data sharing between the Departments of War and Veterans Affairs to speed veterans’ access to benefits and employment opportunities.
  • Mental health breakthroughs: President Trump signed an Executive Order to accelerate access to treatments for serious mental illness — especially for our veterans, who suffer higher rates of serious mental illness and suicide.
  • New careers: President Trump launched Freedom Haulers, a Department of Transportation fast-track program to help service members earn their Commercial Driver’s License.
  • Relief for veterans on fixed incomes: The Working Families Tax Cuts delivered historic tax relief on Social Security for seniors and an unprecedented $50 billion investment to transform rural healthcare.
  • CHAMPVA backlog eliminated: In November 2025, the Trump Administration wiped out the entire CHAMPVA backlog — more than 70,000 unprocessed applications inherited from the Biden Administration.
  • A home for homeless veterans: President Trump signed an Executive Order to improve veterans’ care and accountability, expand options to cut wait times, and establish the National Center for Warrior Independence to house up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028.
  • A first-term promise kept: In his first term, he signed an Executive Order ensuring veterans have seamless access to mental health care and suicide prevention resources as they return to civilian life, especially in the critical first year.

Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Veterans Affairs is delivering for those who served:

  • Housing heroes: More than 95,000 homeless veterans housed in FY2025 and FY2026 — the two highest years on record.
  • Slashing the backlog: The benefits backlog is down nearly 70% since January 20, 2025, and average disability claims processing time is down 46%.
  • Record claims: A record 3.11 million compensation claims processed in FY2026 — up 23.5% from FY2024 — with nearly 94% accuracy.
  • More veterans in care: More than 330,000 new veterans enrolled in VA health care in 2026, and record highs of 82.7 million direct care and 68.1 million community care appointments in FY2026.
  • Care on veterans’ schedules: More than 3.5 million early-morning, evening, and weekend appointments offered since January 20, 2025.
  • Modern facilities: Opened 47 new health care clinics and invested nearly $5 billion in FY2026 to modernize and repair VA facilities — the largest maintenance investment in VA history.
  • Health records back on track: VA’s electronic health record modernization is back on track, now deployed at new sites in Ohio, Kentucky, Michigan, Indiana, and Alaska.
  • Protecting veterans’ homes: Reformed VA home loan protections to keep veterans from losing their homes to foreclosure.

This morning, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth systematically dismantled the desperate, ego-driven impeachment hoax by a disgruntled and defeated Congressman. Secretary Hegseth made clear that every operation targeted in the eight articles was lawful, ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, properly notified to Congress, and carried out by warriors who delivered decisive results. He also made clear that this is not oversight; it is a political spectacle aimed at President Donald J. Trump and the men and women who defend our country.

  • “What one disgruntled and defeated Congressman is attempting is not oversight and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle — a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment, timed for one man’s final days in Congress to try to do damage to this President, this country, and most irresponsibly, the Warriors who defend it. It’s a farce and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it.” (Watch)
  • “In the 250 years of our American Republic, no Secretary of War or Secretary of Defense has ever been impeached for carrying out lawful military operations — and in our case, successful ones at that — not once, War Powers resolution or not. Not under Reagan in Lebanon; not under Clinton in Kosovo; not under Obama in Iraq and Syria; not under Biden in Iraq and Syria. That’s the standard… And one disgruntled Congressman wants to shred it over policy disagreements.” (Watch)
  • “That’s what it is: policy disagreements — not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause. The proper remedy for a policy disagreement? It’s legislation. It’s debate. It’s the next Presidential election. It’s not handing the House and Senate floor to the Democrats so that they can run a show trial against the President and the Secretary of War while Republicans still control Congress and should be delivering wins for the American people.” (Watch)
  • “For the first time in American history, a Cabinet secretary overseeing America’s military is being attacked not for losing conflicts with our enemies, but for winning them. Condemned not for defeat, but for military victory.” (Watch)
  • “As for the articles themselves — Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen — every one was a lawful operation ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress, and executed by American warriors who did their jobs.” (Watch)
  • “This is not about me. Politicians in Washington have accused the sailors and the pilots who struck narcoterrorist boats of war crimes for doing their job. Senators, in cute videos, have suggested the same. This resolution is the next step: put the Secretary on trial today and the men and women who carried out those orders tomorrow. If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me.” (Watch)
  • “We’ve seen this show before. They impeached President Trump over a perfect phone call; they impeached him again in his final week in office. Both times they failed, both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now, they’re trying a third time — this time against a member of his Cabinet. They will fail again.” (Watch)
  • “Let’s be clear about what this resolution actually does. It tells our enemies — Iran, the cartels, every adversary watching — that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations… It puts a target on the backs of American warriors by signaling that Congress will undermine their missions in real time. This is not patriotism; this is sabotage.” (Watch)
  • “In Operation Epic Fury, by every measure, we achieved a historic military victory… We control the Strait of Hormuz. Crazy Islamists in Tehran will never, ever have a nuclear weapon. A historic effort, only made possible by a courageous Commander-in-Chief.” (Watch)
  • “From Day One, President Trump made homeland security national security. We sent American troops to lock down the southwest border and choked off the cartel pipeline of human smuggling, of drugs, and death. Then, we took the fight to them… Thousands of American lives saved with every drug boat sunk and every shipment prevented.” (Watch)
  • “President Trump gave this Department what it has not had in a generation: a Commander-in-Chief with the courage to lead and the resolve to win. I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them — and I would do it again tomorrow.” (Watch)
  • “We will not apologize for putting American lives first. We will not apologize for stopping the flow of drugs that kill our citizens. We will not apologize for destroying the capabilities of a regime that chants ‘death to America.’” (Watch)
  • “We’ve never had a better Commander-in-Chief, full stop. I get to watch him every single day. He lives and breathes America First and it’s the honor of a lifetime to be his Secretary of War.” (Watch)

The support for Secretary Hegseth has been swift and unambiguous:

President Donald J. Trump: “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!”

Vice President JD Vance: “Has Pete Hegseth committed impeachable crimes? The question is absurd and the answer is: obviously not. Like so much of Congress, impeachment has become a ridiculous show that stands in for actual policymaking. Congress has so many tools for registering its policy disagreements. Rather than use them, they’re going to try to impeach Pete Hegseth. They did the same to Donald Trump. Legislation is hard. Impeachments are easy (and ultimately, inconsequential). The irony is that legislators are most angry at Pete on the issues where he’s most correct: repositioning forces away from Europe/Ukraine and reorganizing the general officer corps. This isn’t about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon.”

Speaker of the House of Representatives Mike Johnson: “The impeachment effort is a political gambit for attention… The idea that you would impeach the Secretary of War at a time of international conflict sends a terrible message to our enemies and our allies, and we’re not going to play that game… It’s just purely for people to get attention, and it’s shameful.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “Not only did Pete execute on a direct order from the Commander-in-Chief [who], in our Constitution, is empowered and trusted with the job of keeping Americans safe, but they did it quite effectively…”

Attorney General Todd Blanche: “He is executing on President Trump’s mission… When you hear [this] rhetoric coming out of the Hill that he’s doing something illegal or wrong, that’s not true — and guess what? Every single Congressman knows that… We very much support Pete and we very much support the work that he’s doing working for this Administration.”

Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins: “@SecWar has defended vital U.S. interests and helped inspire record-high recruiting levels in America’s Armed Forces. He’s also been a great partner as @DeptofWar and @DeptVetAffairs work together to support servicemembers as they transition to Veterans. Proud to call him a colleague and friend.”

Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum: “Together with @POTUS, @SecWar has overseen historically successful military operations, for which America, and the entire world, are safer. He has cut red tape to unleash innovation and modernize our military technologies. He has sent thousands of troops to secure the Southern Border. He has deployed the National Guard to make our cities, including our capital, safe again. And he has strengthened relationships with our allies to deter adversaries and protect the United States. This is America-First leadership in action.”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “Secretary Hegseth is doing exactly what President Trump promised for the American people: putting AMERICA FIRST and Making our Military STRONG Again. Our brave men and women in uniform deserve LEADERSHIP focused on defending our nation, not being dragged into political games. Alongside @SecWar: We will stand. We will fight. We will defend this republic.”

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin: “Under the historic leadership of President Trump, @DHSgov has had NO stronger partner on border security than @PeteHegseth and @DeptofWar. Together, we have locked down the border, choked off the cartels’ pipeline, and saved American lives. Pete is a patriot and a warfighter, and I am proud to call him a friend.”

Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner: “Under @SecWar’s leadership, our military has eliminated top threats to our homeland and modernized our warfighting capabilities to protect the American people. Impeaching the Secretary of War for lawful military action sets a dangerous precedent. Congress should be focused on representing and delivering real results for the American people.”

Administrator of the Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler: “Thanks to @SecWar, military recruitment has reached record highs, the U.S. has eliminated dangerous terrorists and cartel leaders around the world, our border is secure, and our warfighters are stronger than ever – that’s what @POTUS promised his Admin would deliver. Secretary Hegseth has also already strengthened our supply chains by recognizing that small businesses comprise over 70% of the defense industrial base and are essential to American military readiness. It is my honor to work with him on our Smaller War Plants Commission, which is making historic investments in small manufacturers to bolster our capabilities, advance innovation, and grow the Arsenal of Freedom that secures peace through strength. I’m proud to stand with @SecWar and this vital mission.”

Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin: “Pete Hegseth is an American patriot and an exceptional Secretary of War! Military recruitment has been hitting record numbers and troop morale has been surging with @PeteHegseth at the tip of the spear.”

Sen. Bernie Moreno: “The idea that a failed Congressman wants to make a political point just because he’s bitter about a defeat is gross.”

Rep. Andrew Clyde: “As a 28-year Navy combat veteran, I know what it takes to protect our nation and preserve our freedoms. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has my full support.”

Rep. Randy Fine: “I trusted Pete Hegseth with my oldest son this summer when he joined the @USNavy. I don’t regret that decision one bit. Thomas Massie’s almost illiterate motion is a fitting disgrace for a petulant loser. Or what I’d expect from someone with the mental capacity of a pinecone. I stand with @SecWar.”

Rep. Nancy Mace: “Vote on Hegseth impeachment is at 5:30pm today – I will not be voting to impeach. The Iran war is through no fault of his own and he should not be the one scapegoated for it. I fully support the changes Hegseth has made to the DoW to make our fighting force the very best it can be.”

Rep. Cory Mills: “I will be supporting our @SecWar as he’s done an amazing job returning our military to its full strength and living the warrior ethos!”

Rep. Ralph Norman: “@SecWar has my full support, and I remain opposed to efforts to impeach him. He has worked tirelessly to restore strength at the Department of War by putting military readiness and our warfighters FIRST. No one has done more to reestablish the strength and credibility of our military on the world stage.”

Rep. Andy Ogles: “I stand with @SecWar… He’s a patriot who has delivered great results for our armed forces.”

Rep. Burgess Owens: “And for years we actually thought Massie was a ‘principled’ Republican… in the end, truth prevails. He’s always been a slick Democrat. Now an unhinged, angry one.”

Rep. William Timmons: “I stand firmly with Secretary Hegseth. Impeachment is one of the most serious powers entrusted to Congress, and Massie’s rush to bring these charges directly to the House floor treats that responsibility like a political stunt.”

Rep. Derrick Van Orden: “Massie is a shameless contrarian who is begging for attention by trying to impeach @secwar before he loses the platform he had as a member of congress. In FOURTEEN YEARS he has never got a bill signed into law. So what the hell has he been doing? Show Boating.”

Rep. Ryan Zinke: “I think it’s a classic case of showboating by a largely discredited, defeated, and disgraced lawmaker—Thomas Massie… I think Pete Hegseth has done a great job. This is unfortunate showboating from Thomas Massie.”

The Wall Street Journal Editorial Board: “Mr. Jeffries may think this is a free vote he can give his left-wingers before Democrats take control in January. But voters will see through this and notice that Democrats are more preoccupied with shooting at Mr. Hegseth than bringing the war in Iran to a victorious end.”

Macdonald-Laurier Institute Senior Fellow Brian L. Cox: “Hey Rep Massie. International law prof & retired military lawyer here. I read the articles of impeachment you filed against @SecWar today. And it’s clear you don’t have a clue what you’re talking about… Each of the articles includes an assertion that SECWAR Hegseth ‘will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office,’ or words to that effect. In reality, the articles of impeachment are a sham – from beginning to end. And it is Rep Massie, not Sec Hegseth, who IS a clear & present threat to the Constitution – for abusing the impeachment powers vested in Congress by distorting international AND domestic law to create the false appearance that Hegseth’s conduct amounts to ‘high Crimes and Misdemeanors.’”

Former White House Chief of Staff Reince Priebus: “What order did Pete Hegseth order or not follow-through on that is impeachable? Massie is a grandstanding axe grinder. This is all for show… There’s nothing here.”

Former Department of Justice Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle: “The War Powers Resolution of 1973 never names the Secretary of War or imposes any duties on him. Charging Hegseth with violating it for executing the President’s orders is a farce and a waste of time. Congress could be doing real work right now instead of staging a political spectacle over a statute that does not even apply to the person they are targeting.”

Fox News Channel Legal Editor Kerri Urbahn: “These Articles of Impeachment, particularly the ones saying that Secretary Hegseth violated the federal statute that talks about notifying Congress and the like, I think they just fall so short.”

The Washington Examiner Chief Political Correspondent Byron York: “Reading through Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. There are 8 articles. Articles 1, 2, and 3 all accuse Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution by waging war in Iran. You might ask yourself: Did Pete Hegseth order US forces into action in Iran? I thought President Trump did that. That’s a good question; from the very beginning, Hegseth appears to serve as a stand-in for Massie’s real desire, which is to impeach Trump… Massie is clearly pushing these articles because he is racing the clock against his own departure from Congress on January 3, having been defeated in a Republican primary in his home state of Kentucky. There is only so much time left to do damage, and with this BS impeachment, Massie is trying to make the most of it.”

Nassau County (NY) Executive Bruce Blakeman: “On the anniversary of the Marine Corps I find it disgraceful that Thomas Massie would move to impeach Pete Hegseth a military veteran and Patriot who restored our military capabilities. Massie is a petulant and small man not worthy of serving in the House of Representatives.”

Veteran Action Founder Mark Lucas: “Side with Massie and Jeffries to impeach Pete Hegseth, and you won’t have a future in the Republican Party. @VeteranAction is watching every vote. Vote NO.”

Veteran Action: “Thomas Massie is a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman. Veteran Action stands with @PeteHegseth. Tell Congress to vote NO on the impeachment.”

Article III Project Founder and President Mike Davis: “This Hegseth impeachment is garbage. Congress declares war. The president makes war. He can repel sudden attack. He can protect American troops, assets, and allies. He does not need a declaration of war. Where were Massie’s articles of impeachment against Lloyd Austin after Afghanistan? They won’t go after Trump. So they go after Pete. Pete Hegseth is a bold and fearless warrior for the Constitution. He is highly effective. He is doing his job. Call your House Rep. Oppose this bogus impeachment.”

Former Deputy National Security Adviser Victoria Coates: “It’s political theater at its worst because the subject is deadly serious. These are our warfighters and they’re being used as pawns. Unfortunately, I think this is a preview of what we’re going to see out of the next Democrat Congress. Congressman Massie should be ashamed of himself for trying to take advantage of these last couple of weeks for this kind of performance.”

NewsNation host Katie Pavlich: “After months of claiming they care about affordability, Democrats in Congress, along with Republican losers like Thomas Massie and Thom Tillis, have their sights focused on Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. They’re demanding impeachment, citing an array of emotional reasons and international law that doesn’t exist… Hegseth is a patriot fulfilling his oath.”

Harvard Law Professor Emeritus Alan Dershowitz: “I would be honored to help defend him because these are not impeachable offenses… None of the grounds that are in the Massie allegations come even close to meeting that standard.”

Attorney Mehek Cooke: “As an attorney my advice to @RepThomasMassie: @SecWar isn’t going anywhere. YOU are. SCOTUS rejected Congress bypassing the President to issue binding orders. You can’t impeach Hegseth for defying an order Congress lacked power to issue. Your articles lack legal foundation.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Will Chamberlain: “Everything about this Hegseth impeachment is like a perfect microcosm of @RepThomasMassie’s passive-aggressiveness, cowardice, resentment, and envy.
– He’s trying to get Hegseth impeached instead of Trump, who he’s still too cowardly to go after personally.
– He’s going after Hegseth because Hegseth endorsed against him in his primary.
– He’s using legal arguments he knows are frivolous. Thomas Massie has been in the House for well over a decade, he knows concurrent resolutions are non-binding, but he’s saying that failing to defy his commander-in-chief and adhere to a non-binding Congressional resolution is an impeachable offense.
– And to top it all off, he’s saying ‘this is all for Hegseth’s own good’ with a smug insinuation that the evidence Massie does not possess will doom him.
– This, from the guy who talked about ‘how much work he and Trump still had to do together’ during his primary, and who published an out-of-date Trump endorsement when Trump had endorsed his opponent.
Thomas Massie is a weak, pathetic excuse for a man.”

Journalist Lara Logan: “The Sec of War has not committed any crime. Massie cannot possibly be so ignorant to the functioning of govt that he does not know the principal military advisors to the President on war in Iran are the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs & the Centcom Commander. So if the Iran war is his issue, he is going after the wrong man. Punishing Pete Hegseth for restoring the U.S. Military to the strength & organization needed to defend this country from all enemies both foreign & domestic is an odd choice. I relish all the attacks that will come at me for saying this – bring it on. Massie is wrong.”

Samaritan’s Purse President Franklin Graham: “I believe the real reason they are coming after Secretary Hegseth is because he has taken on the anti-God, woke, and DEI initiatives that the Biden administration had pushed down the throats of our military. Since Secretary Hegseth has been at the Pentagon, he’s been cleaning house—and millions of Americans are grateful. I encourage everyone to pray for him, that God would give him strength for this difficult hour.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Josh Hammer: “Patriots stand with @PeteHegseth.”

Lieutenant Colonel Robert “Buzz” Patterson, USAF (Ret.): “Massie is trying to impeach him and @PeteHegseth is changing our military for the better! This is huge! I support Pete. He’s a great dude and we need him.”

Center for Renewing America Executive Director Wade Miller: “The good news is that voters already impeached Massie. He was one of the biggest facilitators of big spending in DC all while he fakely postured on it to Americans. His entire sham impeachment effort is merely revenge because Trump endorsed against him. Weaponizing impeachments like this is exceedingly corrupt and Congress will now be less corrupt once Massie is out of office.”

The Dossier Publisher Jordan Schachtel: “Would be beyond absurd for any GOP rep to vote for impeachment. SecWar has done a terrific job revitalizing the military and has served his country admirably.”

Advancing American Freedom Senior Legal Fellow Hans von Spakovsky: “Massie is abusing impeachment power; it’s not intended to be used as political weapon when you disagree with policy but only for serious misconduct”

Article III Project: “Rep. Thomas Massie filed an impeachment resolution against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, and Democrats are itching to run with it. The House must kill it. Hegseth committed no treason. He took no bribe. No evidence shows corruption or any other crime.”

California Post Opinion Editor Joel Pollak: “Impeachment of a cabinet member for doing his job, even badly (not the case here), is unconstitutional. It’s why I opposed the impeachment of the (truly awful) Mayorkas under Biden. Media cheerleaders remind us they are siding with one party — and with America’s enemy in wartime.”

Commentator Glenn Beck: “Pete Hegseth is everything the DC establishment hates, and that’s why they’re making him a scapegoat. He transformed the Department of War from a gay, woke, weak cesspool into a deadly fighting force once again. He has inspired our warriors to serve their country, not their ideology. He has made it clear to our enemies that the United States military will not be mocked. That is his real ‘crime’ against the establishment that was managing America’s decline. They’re trying to make this all about the Iran War. But that’s Trump’s conflict. If you think it’s an illegal war, your argument is with the man we elected as Commander-in-Chief, not the man he chose to run the department.”

Commentator Mark Levin: “Seeking the impeachment of the Secretary of War in the middle of military operations against the Iranian regime, without a single legitimate impeachable allegation, is among the evilest and most diabolical acts of any political majority/party in our history! The entire Democrat Party and a freak Republican on his way out of Congress giving aid and comfort to the enemy– an enemy that has killed and maimed thousands of Americans, sought the assassination of the president and others, and will get nuclear weapons if it is not defeated. History will remember this, depending on how long this republic survives.”

America First Policy Institute: “Under @SECWAR’s leadership, the U.S. military hit a 15-YEAR recruiting high across all 5 branches. Americans are PROUD to wear the uniform and serve our great Nation.”

Tea Party Patriots Co-Founder Jenny Beth Martin: “Hegseth just laid it out. This impeachment push tells Iran and every adversary that we will punish our own warriors for winning a lawful fight. One rogue legislator with a personal grudge does not get to veto the commander in chief. This is not patriotism. This is sabotage.”

Tea Party Patriots: “The House votes at 5:30 tonight on impeaching Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary for re-election, forced the vote. ‘None of these are high crimes or misdemeanors.’ Pete Hegseth is right.”

The post Secretary Hegseth Torches Baseless Impeachment Stunt: “This Is Not Patriotism; This Is Sabotage” appeared first on The White House.
